answer.evidence: The main body is the canopy, a rounded blob. Its silhouette widens from 1 px at row 1 to 28 px at rows 13-20, then narrows to the 6 px trunk by row 33. The upper rows 2-12 are lighter green (#538b42 in column x=15) and read as a lit top. Rows 13-30 are mid and dark green (#2d5b34, #193320), which is the shaded front and underside. There is no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the top reading rests only on the lit dome and the blob silhouette, not on a hard edge. This is a weak top-surface reading. The trunk (6 px wide, rows 30-40) is a vertical face with a light left side and a dark right side. The base patch at rows 41-46 has an oval width profile (12, 19, 23, 25, 23, 19, 12), so it reads as a ground mound seen from above. The object is organic and a tree is not column-like, so no round cap is reported.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small tree with a dark green canopy, a short trunk and a few grass tufts. Its canopy has about 4 green steps with some clump texture, but the clumps are coarse and low-contrast next to the references' leaf clusters. Its outline is a dark green tint with no neutral black (0% near-neutral edge pixels), which matches the references. It has no flat fills (0% near-flat). Density is the weak point: 9 visible tones per tile against 26 and 29 for the references, so it is about a third as rich. The trunk and roots are simple, with few bark or root-flare tones. Both references show many more leaf highlights, bark grain and per-clump shading. The candidate looks flatter and thinner in information than the Beodeul standard.
